title: Japanese 11-Year-Old Wins Esports Gold Medal
paragraphs: Yuki Kurihara, an 11-year-old elementary school student from Tokyo, Japan, won an esports gold medal at the Asian Games in Nagoya on September 26.
Kurihara beat a series of players — some three times his age — before meeting 24-year-old Kang Dongshin of South Korea in the Puyo Puyo Champions final.

Puyo Puyo Champions is a puzzle game in which colored objects called "puyos" fall from the top of the screen. Players have to connect four or more of them in a chain to clear them. Clearing chains of puyos also causes "garbage" puyos to be sent to the opponent, obstructing their play.

Kurihara, who first began playing the game when he was 6, is known for his ability to assess both his own and his opponent's area so that he knows exactly when to clear a chain and send garbage puyos.
"I'm really happy," Kurihara said after receiving his medal. "The gold medal is really beautiful, shiny and heavy."
He said he also liked the little mascot doll he was given for winning.
"The plush toy is super cute, and it's cool that it is gold-colored too."
"It's obvious that my opponent was skilled and above my level," Kang said. "His technical ability and accuracy are incredible."
Kurihara is believed to be the youngest-ever gold medalist in the Asian Games, which have been running since 1951. And he's certainly the youngest in these Asian Games.
Japanese media has reported he trains eight hours a day and still keeps up his grades in school.
Esports was held in the Asian Games for the first time three years ago in Hangzhou, China. It was so popular that tickets were sold by lottery. It's also an audience favorite in Japan.
